recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR-33392. Do not restore the Jira resolution's participant wording into Procedure because it would not match the current Procedure element path; handle FHIR-55015 separately if a broader resolved-change-required reconciliation run includes it.
issue_request: FHIR-33392 was a Published Patient Care change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking how to store the time periods during which each performer participated in a Procedure. The accepted resolution added a 0..1 Period element on the performer/participant backbone for when the participant performed the procedure.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by commit 583cc4cd5aa65894f40d05da91a015ff42ff5617 (J#33392 Add Procedure.performer.period), which inserted Procedure.performer.period with committee note J33392, min 0, max 1, type Period, short text, and definition text in source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml. No prior Issue-Reconcile-Key commit for FHIR-33392 existed on the combined branch before this reconciliation.
additional_context: Procedure is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml is in current build scope. The current source still contains Procedure.performer.period with the requested 0..1 Period cardinality and explanatory short/definition text. The Jira resolution uses participant wording, but the Procedure source model uses the performer backbone, and the applied commit used Procedure.performer.period consistently. A later same-element clarification, FHIR-55015, is only Resolved - change required and is outside this run's default applied/published source-edit scope; it is context only, not a reason to alter the FHIR-33392 audit.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current active Procedure StructureDefinition already provides the element needed to represent the performer-specific period requested by FHIR-33392.
